messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Multivariate issues
parts:
Hi Ben,

I'm attaching both files that were changed:
- src/stan/math/error_handling/matrix/check_pos_definite.hpp
- src/stan/math/matrix/multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose.hpp

The model that tickles the problem is in issue.stan (attached; thanks, Bob).


To summarize, the check_pos_definite() called by log_prob() with the parameters instantiated as stan::agrad::var does not fail in the same way as check_pos_definite() called by write_array() with the parameters instantiated as double.

My guess is that are actual differences in implementation. Rob, want to help me track it down? If so, the way I would tackle it is:
1) make sure the double and stan::agrad::var matrices have the same values. there should be no difference in values.
2) check that Omega is actually a corr_matrix. Maybe we've been too loose there and this is actually propagating some weird behavior.
3) check that diag_pre_multiply(sigma, Omega) has the same results under both var and double. I think this is the same code, so I don't expect this to be the problem, but might as well check.
4) Given the same inputs to multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose() make sure the outputs are the same.
5) make sure the check functions are correct. Perhaps there's something weird going on testing double vs. var. Seems really unlikely, but it's still a place we should look at.

There might be a better way to hunt this down. If you've got a better strategy, go right at it.





Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Multivariate issues
parts:
On Sunday, November 2, 2014 10:50:00 AM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
4) Given the same inputs to multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose() make sure the outputs are the same.

The double version of multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose.hpp is still not numerically equal to the agrad/rev version. We changed the double version to force the result to be symmetric but the fact that it could be numerically asymmetric before implies that it is different than agrad/rev. Also, the symmetricizing operation may result in numerical indefiniteness. So, I think the double version of multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose.hpp just needs to be changed so it is like the agrad/rev version except without calculating the derivatives.

Ben
